The active arm closes with the moral attributes: benevolence (§6.9.1) and righteousness (§6.9.2), God as good in will and just in act. Both are act-attributes before they are value-attributes: to will the good and to render justice is to do something, directed at an object, across the relation between agent and recipient.

Pressed, each requires the directed-crossing structure of any moral act whatever, so that the goodness and justice the tradition locates in a being beyond Nature are found instead in the structured agency T, S, and Φ underwrite.
